one_liner: Header-only C++11 port of the Flatbush packed Hilbert R-tree for static 2D boxes; no measured head-to-head win over any baseline.
what_it_does: A static spatial index for 2D points and axis-aligned rectangles: add items to a FlatbushBuilder<T>, call finish() once, then run bounding-box search() and k-nearest-neighbour neighbors() queries that return item ids, with optional filter callbacks, result limits, a max distance and a custom lower-bound distance metric. T can be int8/uint8/int16/uint16/int32/uint32/float/double. The serialized buffer uses the JavaScript library's layout (format v3), so indexes can be exchanged with mourner/flatbush, rebuilt with from(), or used in place over a memory-mapped buffer with fromView(). It is not a drop-in for Boost.Geometry rtree or any other C++ index; the API mirrors the JS library.
how_it_is_fast: Items are sorted by the Hilbert-curve value of their box centres (quantized to a 16-bit grid) and packed bottom-up into a fixed-fanout tree (default node size 16) stored in one flat array, so there are no per-node allocations or pointers. The build uses a custom partial quicksort that only orders items down to node granularity, plus a bucket pass, and computes Hilbert indices with SIMD (SSE2 up to AVX-512, chosen at compile time). Queries test node boxes with SIMD comparisons, prefetch child nodes, and kNN uses a priority queue over node distances.
when_to_use: Read-mostly 2D datasets (map features, tiles, bounding boxes of shapes) that are built once and queried many times, from thousands to millions of items.
Sharing or memory-mapping a prebuilt index, including indexes produced by the JavaScript Flatbush, without a copy (fromView on an aligned buffer).
Projects that want a single header with no dependencies and C++11 support, installable from Conan Center or vcpkg.
Range queries returning few hits (the README's 1000 searches at 0.01% area take 2 ms total on an i7-1185G7) and small-k nearest-neighbour lookups.
when_not_to_use: Data that changes after building: there is no insert or delete; any change means a full rebuild.
3D or higher-dimensional data, or non-box geometry predicates (polygons, segments): it indexes 2D axis-aligned boxes only.
Choosing on proven speed over Boost.Geometry rtree, nanoflann or GEOS STRtree: the repo benchmarks only itself and publishes no comparison with any C++ or JS baseline.
Very large single kNN result sets: the README's 1 search of 1,000,000 neighbours takes 86-88 ms with gcc/clang, no better than the JS original's 84 ms on a different machine.
Inputs above uint32 item counts: numItems is stored as uint32_t and the builder throws std::length_error past the format limits.

integration.dependencies: none (Google Benchmark, GoogleTest and fuzztest are fetched by CMake only for benchmarks and tests)
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (uses std::span automatically in C++20); README table built with clang 18.1.3, gcc 13.3.0 and MSVC 19.29
integration.platforms: any C++11 target; SIMD paths for x86/x86-64 (SSE2 default on x64, SSE3/SSSE3/SSE4/AVX/AVX2/AVX-512 by compiler flags) with a scalar fallback elsewhere; a 32-bit compile failure was fixed in issue #14 (closed 2026-09-25)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; search() and neighbors() are const and the header declares no mutable members, so concurrent queries on a built index look safe (inferred from source, not stated); the builder is not shared-safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same serialized format and near-identical API to the JavaScript Flatbush, but not a drop-in for any C++ spatial index

gotchas: Errors are reported with exceptions (std::invalid_argument, std::length_error): wrong template type for a buffer, misaligned fromView buffer, empty builder, oversized index. Builds with -fno-exceptions need care.

The SIMD level is fixed at compile time from compiler flags (#pragma message prints which one); the default on x64 is only SSE2, so pass -mavx2 or /arch:AVX2 for the faster paths, and keep the same flags and FLATBUSH_SPAN setting across translation units.

Integer coordinate types had a SIMD bug: updateBounds stored only the minimum values (issue #9, closed 2026-06-27), corrupting node boxes so queries missed items; use a release after that fix if you index int types. Earlier issues: a multiple-definition link error (#2) and search/neighbors not compiling on 32-bit targets (#14), both closed.
A custom distance callback must return a lower bound of the point-to-box distance, and it bypasses the SIMD path; fromView requires the buffer to outlive the index and stay unchanged.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over the JavaScript Flatbush when the consumer is C++ (the formats are interchangeable), and over nanoflann or tidwall/rtree.c when you need a static box index (not just points) with zero-copy loading of a prebuilt buffer. If you need updates, 3D or measured speed against Boost.Geometry, GeoToolbox KdBoxTree, PH-tree or nanoflann have published comparisons and this does not.
verified_claims_summary: The repo makes no speedup claim; its README table reports only its own Google Benchmark timings on an i7-1185G7 (clang 18.1.3 / gcc 13.3.0 / MSVC 19.29, CMake Release, SIMD level unstated): index 1M rectangles 55-72 ms, 1000 searches at 1% area 17-18 ms, 1 search of 1M neighbours 63-88 ms. Comparing with the JS original's README (M1 Pro, Node v24) gives only cross-machine directional ratios (about 2x on build, about 3.7x on 1% searches, none on the 1M-neighbour kNN).
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-03, 161 commits, CI with unit, fuzz, CodeQL and benchmark jobs), MIT-licensed single header, packaged on Conan Center and vcpkg; evidence tier D because nothing is measured against a baseline.
